title: SF deploys flood barriers, 35,000 sandbags for residents
text:
SF deploys flood barriers, 35,000 sandbags for residents - ABC7 San Francisco 
 24/7 Live San Francisco East Bay South Bay Peninsula North Bay Live WEATHER 
 Live storm updates: Severe flooding inundates roadways leads to crashes, closures across Bay Area 
 By ABC7 Bay Area Digital Staff Last updated: Friday, November 20, 2026 3:54AM GMT 
 Stream local breaking news and original programming, live 24/7, from ABC7 Bay Area. Record-breaking rainfall left much of San Francisco underwater on Wednesday as a Level 3 storm dumped several inches of rain across the region.
 Videos sent to ABC7 Eyewitness News showed residents wading through knee-deep water and cars trying to navigate flooded roadways.
 LIVE: Track rain in San Francisco Bay Area with Live Doppler 7 
 Downtown San Francisco also saw a record amount of rainfall. The 2.31 inches of rain recorded was the highest for Nov. 18, breaking a record set in 1918.
 The average rainfall in San Francisco for the whole month of November is 2.6 inches, according to the weather service.
 According to ABC7 meteorologist Drew Tuma, the storm will move out of the region on Thursday, but there is still a chance of thunderstorms throughout the day.
 There is also a slight chance of waterspouts over the ocean and brief rotating storms along the coast that could produce isolated tornadoes on land, although those are considered secondary threats, according to the NWS.

 Here's how the news is developing. 51 Updates By J.R. Stone Nov 18, 2026, 7:25 AM GMT 
 SF deploys flood barriers, 35,000 sandbags for residents 
 San Francisco officials are preparing for an approaching storm by deploying flood barriers, stocking sandbags and clearing storm drains in some of the city's most flood-prone areas. San Francisco officials are preparing for an approaching storm by deploying flood barriers, stocking sandbags and clearing storm drains in some of the city's most flood-prone areas.
 The city has stockpiled 35,000 sandbags and has been distributing them six days a week, officials said.
 One of the city's longest temporary flood barriers has been installed at 17th and Folsom streets, an area known for flooding because it is among the lowest inland points in San Francisco.
 "Farther back it's gotten about this high so we've had to lift everything up, everything," said Issac Hanley of Lutz Plumbing Inc., describing previous flooding at his business.
 Hanley said the company relies on a high-powered sump pump to manage floodwaters.
 "This pump is activated when the water gets to a certain height and then it shoots water out of here," Hanley said.
 While flood barriers have been put in place, Hanley questioned how effective they will be in preventing flooding.
 "Honestly, it doesn't really help. In my opinion. We flood from the inside out," Hanley said. "It's all from the street, it doesn't happen just because it's raining hard, if stuff was cleared then we would be fine."
 Nearby storm drains still contained some debris, but city officials said crews have been working to clear them ahead of the storm.
 "We had about, in the last couple of days with the storm, about 80 storm drains cleared," said Rachel Gordon of San Francisco Public Works.
 The San Francisco Fire Department is also urging residents to take precautions if flooding occurs.
 "We want to advise people to avoid driving through standing water. We can't see that if there's potholes or maybe a discarded bicycle or something like that that could damage a vehicle and leave you stranded in rising water," said Capt. Jack Ayers.
 Officials also caution against driving electric vehicles, bicycles or scooters through standing salt water because of the risk of fire.
 Hanley said his business has taken steps to protect valuable inventory ahead of the storm, as it has during previous flooding events.
 "Just try to pump it out quicker than it comes," Hanley said.
 Caltrans said its crews are working around the clock and will be prepared to respond to emergencies with sandbags, pumps and other equipment if needed.
 By Suzanne Phan Nov 18, 2026, 1:43 AM GMT 
 San Francisco braces for major storm 
 City crews, business owners and residents across San Francisco spent Tuesday preparing for a major storm expected to arrive Wednesday. City crews, business owners and residents across San Francisco spent Tuesday preparing for a major storm expected to arrive Wednesday, with flood barriers in place, storm drains being cleared and sandbags distributed ahead of the anticipated weather.
 Along the Embarcadero, the Port of San Francisco has installed a large barricade in preparation for high tides and King Tides expected in the coming weeks. Officials described the barrier as a temporary measure designed to help reduce flooding associated with El Niño and elevated water levels.
 Across the city, residents took precautions based on lessons learned from previous storms.
 In the Mission District, business owner Robert Davis stacked sandbags in the doorway of his amplifier business after experiencing flooding on 17th Street in the past.
 "It was pretty bad actually. I think it was a foot up here," Davis said.
 Other businesses near Folsom and 17th streets installed metal barricades as an additional defense against rising water. Flood barriers have also been returned to several known flooding hotspots in the neighborhood. According to city officials, some businesses in the area experienced 3 to 4 feet of flooding in 2023.
 San Francisco Public Works Director Rachel Gordon said city crews have been preparing extensively for the storm.
 "We are ready for this," Gordon said.
 Public Works crews have focused on clearing storm drains and addressing other storm-related hazards.
 "Our street crews are out cleaning the storm drains; they want to keep leaves and litter out of the storm drain," Gordon said.
 The city has also deployed tree crews to reduce the risk of storm-related damage.
 "We do have our tree crews out right now proactively pruning trees that look vulnerable to failure," Gordon said.
 At the San Francisco Public Works Operations Yard on Kansas and Marin streets, residents formed long lines to pick up free sandbags. The city said approximately 35,000 sandbags are available, with each customer eligible to receive up to 10.
 Among those waiting was Ingleside resident Eric Lopez, who said his garage flooded during a previous storm.
 "It got into the garage--half way into the garage -- like about half inch of water," Lopez said. "I anticipate it's going to be a lot more this time."
 Bayview resident Ralph Coleman also picked up sandbags after dealing with flooding concerns near his home.
 "I got a low door at my house. Sometimes the water comes up to it," Coleman said.
 Coleman said drainage issues can quickly worsen flooding in his neighborhood.
 "If they don't clean the gutters and the drains, it will get bad," he said.
 To avoid a last-minute rush, Coleman collected sandbags for both himself and a neighbor.
 "I'm trying to get it early," he said.
 Meanwhile, the Port of San Francisco's 4-foot-tall flood barrier remains in place along part of the Embarcadero as city agencies monitor forecasts for heavy rain, high tides and storm-related flooding.
 Officials are urging residents to be prepared. For non-life-threatening problems such as flooding, clogged storm drains, sewer backups or potentially hazardous trees, residents can call 311 or use the city's mobile app. Anyone who encounters a downed power line is advised to call 911.
 The San Francisco Public Utilities Commission is also encouraging residents to monitor storm information through the city's storm preparedness resources and to sign up for emergency alerts.
 As the city braces for Wednesday's storm, officials say preparation and early action can help minimize impacts from flooding and other weather-related hazards.
 By Dryden Quigley Nov 18, 2026, 1:29 AM GMT 
 Oakland urges residents to prepare for storm 
 Oakland residents are being urged to prepare for heavy rain, strong winds, possible flooding and power outages ahead of the storm. Oakland residents are being urged to prepare for heavy rain, strong winds, possible flooding and power outages ahead of a storm expected to bring some of its strongest impacts to the East Bay hills.
 The Oakland Zoo said it will be closed to daytime visitors on Wednesday and will decide that day whether to open Glowfari.
 In Oakland, resident Jonathan Svilar said he is taking precautions after dealing with flooding in the past.
 "When we first moved into our place, my entire basement office got flooded by about six inches of water. So I'm really just trying to avoid that," Svilar said.
 Oakland Fire Department spokesperson Michael Hunt said city officials are preparing for a range of potential impacts, including flooding, mudslides and power outages.
 "City leadership and city departments have been meeting on a daily basis to address what the city can do," Hunt said.
 Hunt encouraged residents to sign up for AC Alerts, charge electronic devices, assemble emergency supplies, and a 'go bag' before conditions worsen.
 "We want to make sure people have all the things they need to survive and support themselves for upwards of 72 hours," Hunt said.
 Oakland residents can obtain up to 10 sandbags and 20 feet of plastic sheeting to help protect their homes from storm damage. Supplies are available at city distribution sites at 5921 Shepherd Canyon Road and 7101 Edgewater Drive. Residents with questions can call 510-615-5566.
 Resident Michael McBride welcomed the effort.
 "I think it's great, anything to avoid some kind of a catastrophe of some sort," McBride said.
 Svilar said the sandbags could help divert water away from vulnerable areas around his home.
 "I have a couple of places around the outside of my house that I know is going to have a little bit of extra water running down. And I just being able to edge it away from the house will be really helpful," he said.
 Power outages are also possible during the storm. PG &E spokesperson Tamar Sarkissian said utility crews are preparing to respond.
 "We make sure that our crews are out there and oftentimes in the rain and wind, just making sure we get the power turned back on safely," Sarkissian said.
 Oakland officials are also asking residents to report clogged storm drains by calling 311 if they cannot safely clear them themselves. Residents should call 911 for downed power lines or other life-threatening emergencies.
 Nov 18, 2026, 12:14 AM GMT 
 Where to pick up sandbags to prepare for Level 3 storm, El Niño 
 Cities around the Bay Area are offering free sandbags to residents to help subsidize the cost of preparing for historically wet weather driven by El Niño this season, with rain in the forecast for most of the next 10 days.
 Oakland residents can pick up pre-filled sandbags at the Municipal Service Center at 7101 Edgewater Drive. The center is open from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday and until 4:30 p.m. on weekends.
 Sandbags are also available in Oakland at the Drainage Services Facility at 5921 Shepherd Canyon Road from 7 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. on weekdays only.
 In San Francisco, residents and business owners in the city can pick up sandbags at the Public Works Operations Yard at 2323 Cesar Chavez St. from 8 a.m. to 2 p.m., every day except Sunday. Enter at Kansas Street and Marin Street.
 San Francisco Public Works will make sandbags available at different locations in the city on upcoming Saturdays with its "Sandbag Saturdays" program. Those giveaways run from 8 a.m. to 2 p.m.
 This Saturday, department personnel will set up at the Marina Green Triangle, in the Marina District, and stairwells 4-7 at the Ocean Beach parking lot, located on the Great Highway at Balboa Street.
 On Dec. 5, crews will be in the South of Market neighborhood, on Sherman Street between Folsom and Harrison streets, and at the Mission District Fire Training Center, at 19th and Folsom streets.
 San Jose residents can pick up sandbags from the Santa Clara Valley Water District at multiple locations in the city. Many sites require residents to fill them, but others offer pre-filled bags.
 Filled bags can be picked up at the City Central Service Yard, at 1661 Senter Road. Unfilled bags with sand available are also available at the Santa Clara Valley Water District Winfield Warehouse at 5812 Winfield Blvd., County East Yard at 1505 Schallenberger Road, and City Maybury Yard at 1404 Maybury Road.
 A map of locations throughout Santa Clara County is available at https://www.valleywater.org/flooding-safety/flood-ready/sandbags .
 Proof of residency is required at many of the sites, and there is a limit of 10 bags per person.
